ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a small ball of mass $m$ is suspended from point $O$ by a thin string of length $l$. The string is pulled straight into a horizontal position, and the ball is given a downward velocity to make it move downward. There is a nail at point $D$ directly below $O$. When the ball reaches point $B$, it will perform circular motion with $D$ as the center and pass through point $C$. It is known that $O D = \frac{2}{3}l$.

1. As the small ball moves from point $A$ to point $C$, by how much does the gravitational potential energy decrease?
2. As the small ball moves from point $A$ to point $C$, how much work is done by gravity?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, a small ball of mass $m$ is suspended from point $O$ by a thin string of length $l$. The string is pulled straight into a horizontal position, and the ball is given a downward velocity to make it move downward. There is a nail at point $D$ directly below $O$. When the ball reaches point $B$, it will perform circular motion with $D$ as the center and pass through point $C$. It is known that $OD=\frac{2}{3}l$. 1. As the small ball moves from point $A$ to point $C$, by how much does the gravitational potential energy decrease? 2. As the small ball moves from point $A$ to point $C$, how much work is done by gravity?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the small ball is at point A on the left side, and A and the suspension point O are on the same horizontal line; the thin string is connected horizontally from A to O. There is a point D directly below O, and the dashed vertical line passes through O, C, D, and B; the distance from O to D is marked in the figure as \(\frac{2}{3}l\). The small ball moves downward from A, and after reaching B the thin string is blocked by the nail at D, and then it makes a smaller circular motion around D; C is located above D and is the upper-end position of this small circle with D as the center. Reasoning: The original rope length is \(l\), and when the small ball reaches B, \(OB=l\). Since \(OD=\frac{2}{3}l\), the radius when rotating around the nail D is \(DB=OB-OD=l-\frac{2}{3}l=\frac{1}{3}l\). C is the upper endpoint of the small circle with D as the center, so \(DC=\frac{1}{3}l\). Thus the vertical distance from C to O is \(OC=OD-DC=\frac{2}{3}l-\frac{1}{3}l=\frac{1}{3}l\). A and O are at the same height, so the vertical descent height of the small ball from A to C is \(\frac{1}{3}l\). The decrease in gravitational potential energy is \(mg\Delta h=mg\cdot\frac{1}{3}l=\frac{1}{3}mgl\). The work done by gravity is equal to the decrease in gravitational potential energy, so the work done by gravity is also \(\frac{1}{3}mgl\).
